claims.text: At tag stage-0, docs/team/meeting-notes-example.md puts three lines directly under its title, before the first section heading: `Mục đích` (the purpose), `Người dự` (who attended) and `Thời lượng` (the duration).
That file states the purpose as deciding whether a `paid` order may be cancelled, lists four attendees (product owner, two developers, a tester) and fixes the duration at twenty minutes.
Under `Quyết định` the file records two short sentences: a `paid` order cannot be cancelled from the application, and the customer has to ask for a refund.

Under `Lý do` the file gives the reason: a refund has to be matched against what the payment gateway recorded, the team has not built that part, and cancelling without refunding would leave an order both cancelled and paid, a state nobody handles.
Under `Việc phải làm` the file holds a table of exactly three rows with the columns `Việc`, `Ai` and `Khi nào`; two rows go to Dev 1 and Dev 2 `Trong sprint này`, the third to PO `Trước sprint sau`.
The heading after that table is `Câu chưa trả lời`, holding one unsettled question — what a `shipped` order the customer refuses counts as — and naming the person who will go and ask.
The file's last section quotes a status update of three lines — `Đang làm`, `Vướng`, `Tiếp theo` — and says those three lines can stand in for a meeting.
The file's closing sentence states the rule for problems: raise them early with an option, not late with an apology.
Four people for twenty minutes is over an hour of the team's time, spent at the same moment (4 × 20 phút, lines 4-5).
claims.source_hint: arithmetic on the attendee count and duration in docs/team/meeting-notes-example.md at stage-0, lines 4-5

claims.text: A meeting needs a purpose, an output and somebody writing the output down. The purpose is what says when the meeting is finished; the time box only says when it has to stop. Without a record, nothing reaches anyone who was not in the room.
claims.source_hint: outline item 1 of the lesson entry in content/tracks/management/track.yaml

claims.text: A meeting's output only reaches people outside the room once somebody writes it down — a note, the story, a chat message. A decision nobody wrote down is one the team can end up making again, differently, later; the reason behind it is the part a later reader cannot reconstruct.
claims.source_hint: outline item 2; docs/team/meeting-notes-example.md at stage-0 writes `Lý do` as its own section under the decision

claims.text: When a question has one obvious owner, writing it (chat, the story, a pull request description) costs less than meeting: the person asked answers when they next look at their messages, and the answer stays where the next person looks. A meeting is worth its cost when talking unlocks the answer.
claims.source_hint: outline item 1 of the lesson entry in content/tracks/management/track.yaml

claims.text: In a three-line status update, the blocked line is usually the one another person has to clear; the doing line matters when it hands work over and the next line when somebody waits on its date.
claims.source_hint: outline item 3; docs/team/meeting-notes-example.md at stage-0 lines 33-35 and 37, which call the three lines a replacement for a meeting

claims.text: A disagreement belongs to the open question and takes the form of a reason about the work, not a preference; once the decision is written the team treats the argument as closed, and reopening it needs something new rather than the old argument.
claims.source_hint: outline item 4; docs/team/meeting-notes-example.md at stage-0 lines 13-15 record the argument as a reason under `Lý do`

claims.text: A new person asking what was just decided and what they do next costs the meeting almost nothing, because the answer has to exist anyway and others in the room are often unsure too; staying quiet is how a room leaves with several different understandings of one decision.
claims.source_hint: outline misconception 1 of the lesson entry in content/tracks/management/track.yaml

claims.text: A problem raised while there is still time is a question the team answers, and the answer can still change what the team builds this sprint; the same problem raised at the end is a missed commitment, which is the one that gets discussed.
claims.source_hint: outline misconception 2; docs/team/meeting-notes-example.md at stage-0 lines 37-38 state the early-with-an-option rule

claims.text: Writing an open question down costs a line, and a question nobody wrote down has to be asked again, often in another meeting; `Câu chưa trả lời` is where the note keeps it.
claims.source_hint: outline item 2; docs/team/meeting-notes-example.md at stage-0 lines 25-27 keep the unsettled question and its owner in the note
